target_customer: Hospital and academic clinical research teams and research networks that must assemble study datasets from EHRs, notes, wearables and surveys
problem: Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems, reading notes chart by chart and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B software and forward-deployed AI deployment sold to research teams, deployed inside each team's own environment (pricing not public)
product_category: Healthcare research data preparation, clinical data abstraction

founders.name: Ritvik Panuganti
founders.background_notes: YC page lists published clinical research, a 300-participant IRB-approved concussion study at Georgia Tech and a VR concussion tool prepared for an FDA 510(k) submission.

founders.name: Supratik Panuganti
education: Georgia Tech, CS and Math (dropped out)
previous_startups: Unnamed AI security company backed by a16z Speedrun (exited, per YC page; company not named)
founders.background_notes: The two founders are brothers who say they built together for 4 years.

competitors.name: Century Health
competitors.what: AI platform (CHARM) that builds research-ready datasets from EHR records for real-world evidence
competitors.traction_then: Reported 97 percent abstraction accuracy against human experts (company claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: Linking records across EHR, REDCap and wearable sources and applying study rules with traceability is standard AI integration work with hard parts in per-site deployment and accuracy, rather than research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Reusable study rules and per-institution deployments create some lock-in, but several funded vendors sell the same abstraction wedge and the product is software on top of general models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say. Funded abstraction vendors and large data players were already active in 2026 and no incumbent action against Sutrix is public.

market_need_then: Company states research teams lose weeks to months per study on data prep and claims paying teams at 10+ institutions cut prep by 80 percent. Industry press in 2025 and 2026 covers clinical data abstraction as a recognized bottleneck. These are company claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses sutrix.ai; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Not described by sources beyond a clean wordmark
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and outcome-led: Turn messy patient data into study-ready datasets

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand was found; the name is similar to Suntrix, Sentrix and Sytrex, which appear in search results instead.

outcome_analysis: Sutrix is a Fall 2026 YC company that is active and far too young for an outcome. Its early strengths are founders with clinical research access at HSS and Emory and a claim of paying institutional customers, while the risks are funded abstraction competitors and long healthcare sales cycles. No outcome search result concerns this company.
notes: No round could be verified. Dealroom (app.dealroom.co/companies/sutrix_yc_f26) shows a $125k seed entry with no investors, a single aggregator figure, so it is not recorded as a round. That Dealroom profile also describes the company as a yoga teacher tool, which conflicts with the YC page and company site, so it was disregarded. Outcome search found nothing about this company. The company website says paying status is unclear: it lists Emory, Georgia Tech, BlueRock and others without saying who pays. Undated competitors (Brim Analytics, Q-Centrix) were left out of the competitor list because no source date was available; they are context only.
